verdicts.reason: The card says it will build DDR3 capacities 'the majors never made or have stopped making'. That is false for both SKUs. Intelligent Memory's Oct-2024 DDR3 flyer and its product page list 32GB DDR3 RDIMM and LRDIMM modules built on its own 8Gb DDR3 parts, plus 16GB SO-DIMMs, which it has shipped since 2014. Samsung, SK hynix and Micron made the 8Gb dual-die DDR3 that 32GB RDIMMs use before those parts went EOL, so new and recovered supply of this exact module already exists (all via search snippets). The card cites no evidence for it, and the canonical landscape contradicts it. TAA treats Korean and Taiwanese DRAM as compliant, COTS is exempt from the BAA component test, memory pays 0% under Section 232, and hi-rel buyers already pay 10-100x for MCMs built on foreign die (01_LANDSCAPE.md 0 item 7, 7.3). The card itself puts GM at ~0% without the premium. The supply side is unproven too. Manassas takes no outside customers (6.1 row 2). The concept comes back only if two things happen: a written program requirement for U.S.-fabbed and U.S.-packaged DRAM, and a SpecTek 'yes' on Manassas wafers.
